spatial_entity.notes: Reuses the existing reviewed spatial identity and its four independently reviewed Cliopatria time-slice geometries. Geometry describes political extent for navigation/context; it does not imply uniform slavery prevalence across every province.

claim.summary: Specialist scholarship treats Rome in the central Roman period and early Empire as a slave society in which slavery was structurally embedded in household, productive, commercial and elite-surplus relations. The strongest generalizations apply above all to Rome and the Italian core, while the institution existed to varying degrees across subject territories. The atlas therefore records a strong positive slavery/enslavement designation for the early-Principate polity slice without treating the whole imperial polygon as uniform in prevalence or assigning a new post-M1 P-level.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy claim ce2feb0a-917f-4bf1-9561-3d1f1f9887d4 into current post-M1 semantics. Legacy P4 is preserved only in historical release lineage and is not copied into this new research claim. Existing reviewed geometry IDs are frozen in data/research/recovery/atlas_expansion_01/recovery_inventory.json.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive institutional/structural classification. Do not infer one empire-wide prevalence level, demographic share or homogeneous labor regime from the political polygon. Italy/core evidence is especially strong; provincial variation is explicit in the specialist synthesis.
